instructions: Start the rice. Cook 1 1/2 cups of basmati rice following the package directions.
Wash the okra and dry it well. Trim the ends and cut each pod in half lengthwise, then into 3/4 inch pieces. Finely chop the onion, tomato, ginger and green chilies.
Heat 2 tbsp of the coconut oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes, until lightly browned.
Add the ginger and green chilies and stir for 1 minute.
Add the okra and cook for 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until tender-crisp. Add the tomato and cook for 1 minute.
Turn the heat to low. Add the turmeric, coriander, chili powder and salt, and stir for 1 minute, until it smells toasty.
Pour in the coconut milk, keeping back 1/3 cup, and add 1/2 cup of water. Bring it to a simmer and cook on low for 3 minutes. Don't let it boil hard. Coconut milk can split.
Stir in the 1/3 cup of coconut milk, the garam masala and the black pepper. Take the pan off the heat.

In a small pan, heat the last 1 tbsp coconut oil over medium-high heat. Add the mustard seeds and wait until they splutter. Add the dried chilies and 2 sprigs of curry leaves and stir for 1 minute. Stand back a little. It will spatter.
Pour the hot oil mixture over the okra.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Nish Kitchen (5 from 52) leads: okra browned with onion, ginger and chilies, then tomato, ground spices and coconut milk simmered briefly, finished with garam masala and a mustard and curry leaf tempering. PlatterShare agrees on frying the okra first and keeping the heat low once coconut milk goes in, and adds whole spices and ginger-garlic paste, which are left out here. Amounts are scaled up from the lead's 10 okra to 12 oz so it feeds four with rice. Needs no soaking or grinding.
